newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine banks urged to lend more to manufacturing.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine banks urged to lend more to manufacturing.

text.p: Ukrainian banks must increase long-term loans and actively support investment projects in order to revive the lagging production sector, Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko said in parliament on Tuesday.

"A large problem is the lack of a considered credit policy. Banks don't think about this, or give long-term loans," Lazarenko said in presenting the government's three-year economic plan, chiefly aimed at reviving Ukraine's production.
Lazarenko said only three percent of all bank loans are long-term, and that only one bank was giving them.
"That is all that we have with which to renew our economy, and as for investment loans, there are practically none."
Lazarenko blamed an under-developed banking system for the limited loan market, and for problems in safeguarding the stability of the new hryvnia currency introduced on September 2.
"There is a lack of pragmatic thinking, and banks think like bookkeepers," Lazarenko said.
The prime minister also criticised the National Bank of Ukraine, saying that its independent policies contributed to many problems in the banking sector.
He gave no details but the government and bank have long been at loggerheads over the government's belief that banks should issue long-term loans.
Lazarenko said although currency reform was complete, the next task was to stabilise the hryvnia and make it fully convertible.

The hryvnia was 1.774 to the dollar on the Ukraine Interbank Currency Exchange on Tuesday from 1.770 on Monday. It began to slip last week from the 1.76 level it had held, with central bank intervention, since its introduction.
Lazarenko also criticised the bank sector for not yet stepping into the international banking world, and for not yet having earned a credit rating.
"The government is working actively in this direction with foreign funding bodies, and has some profitable agreements," he said.
Lazarenko said the government was ready to meet the central bank and provide support to banks with long-term loans.
